text:
The major product in the following reaction is :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The most acidic proton in adenine is the imidazole N–H at N-9 ($\text{p}K_{a}\approx 9.8$); the $\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$ protons are far less acidic, so the base removes the N-9 proton and forms the adeninide anion.

The anion attacks $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{I}$ in an $S_{N}2$ reaction through N-9, giving neutral 9-methyladenine.

A ring-methylated cation that still carries an N–H would lose that proton in the basic medium, so a cationic product is not formed, and the exocyclic $\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$ is a poor nucleophile because its lone pair is delocalised into the pyrimidine ring.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
The calculated spin-only magnetic moments
(BM) of the anionic and cationic species of
[$Fe(H_{2}O)_{6}$]$_{2}$[$Fe(CN)_{6}$], respectively, are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}_{2}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]$ the cation is $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$ and the anion is $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{4-}$; iron is $+2$ ($3d^{6}$) in both.

Anion: $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ is a strong-field ligand, so the $d^{6}$ electrons pair as $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$; $n=0$ and $μ=0$.

Cation: $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ is a weak-field ligand, so $d^{6}$ is high spin, $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$, with $n=4$:

$μ=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{24}=4.90\text{BM}$

The magnetic moments of the anionic and cationic species are 0 and 4.9 BM respectively.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot

text:
Among the following molecules / ions,
$C_{2}^{2-},N_{2}^{2-},O_{2}^{2-},O_{2}$
which one is diamagnetic and has the shortest
bond length?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Note : 

(1) $\, ~$ Bond strength $\propto$ Bond order 

(2) $\, ~$ Bond length $\propto$ $\frac{1}{Bondorder}$

(3) [MATH$_$FAILED] Bond order $=\frac{1}{2}$ [$N_{b}$ $-$ $N_{a}$] 

$N_{b} =$ No of electrons in bonding molecular orbital 

$N_{a}$ $=$ No of electrons in anti bonding molecular orbital 

(4) $\, ~$ upto 14 electrons, molecular orbital configuration is 


[IMG]


Here $N_{a} =$ Anti bonding electron $=$ 4 and $N_{b} = 10$

(5) $\, ~$ After 14  electrons to 20 electrons molecular orbital configuration is - - -


[IMG]


Here $N_{a} = 10$

and $N_{b} = 10$

(A) In O atom 8 electrons present, so in $O_{2},  8$ $\times$ 2 = 16 electrons present. 

Then in $O_{2}^{2-}$ no of electrons = 18

$\therefore \quad$ Molecular orbital configuration of $O_{2} (16$ electrons) is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }$ $σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }$ $σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{1}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{1}}^{\ast }$

$\therefore \quadN_{a} = 6$

$N_{b} = 10$

$\therefore \quad$ BO = $\frac{1}{2}[10-6]=2$

Here 2 unpaired electrons are present so it is paramagnetic.

(D) Molecular orbital configuration of O ${}_{2}^{2-}$ (18 electrons) is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}^{\ast }$

$\therefore \quad$ $N_{b} = 10$

$N_{a} = 8$

$\therefore \quad$ BO = $\frac{1}{2}$ [ 10 $-$ 8] = 1

Here no unpaired electrons are present so it is diamagnetic.

(B)   $C_{2}^{2-}$ has 14 electrons. 

Molecular orbital configuration of $C_{2}^{2-}$ is

 $σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}$

$\therefore \quadN_{a} = 4$

$N_{b} = 10$

$\therefore \quad$ BO = $\frac{1}{2}[10-4]=3$

Here no unpaired electron present, so it is diamagnetic.

(C)   $N_{2}^{2-}$ has 16 electrons. 

Molecular orbital configuration of $N_{2}^{2-}$ is

 $σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{1}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{1}}^{\ast }$

$\therefore \quadN_{a} = 6$

$N_{b} = 10$

$\therefore \quad$ BO = $\frac{1}{2}[10-6]=2$

Here 2 unpaired electron present, so it is paramagnetic.

As Bond length $\propto$ $\frac{1}{Bondorder}$

so among two diamagnetic ions $C_{2}^{2-}$ and $O_{2}^{2-}$, bond order of $C_{2}^{2-}$ is more so it will have shorter bond length.

text:
5 moles of an ideal gas at 100 K are allowed
to undergo reversible compression till its
temperature becomes 200 K.
If $C_{V} = 28 JK^{–1}$mol$^{–1}$, calculate $\Delta$U and $\Delta$pV for
this process. $(R = 8.0 JK^{–1}$ mol$^{–1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For ideal gas,

$\Delta U = nC_{v}\Delta$T

= 5 $\times$ 28 $\times$ (200 - 100)

= 14 kJ

We know,

PV = nRT

$\therefore$ $\Delta$(PV) = nR$\Delta$T = 5 $\times$ 8 $\times$ 100 = 4 kJ

text:
For a reaction scheme $A⟶^{k_{1}}B⟶^{k_{2}}C$,

 if
the rate of formation of B is set to be zero then
the concentration of B is given by :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,
the rate of formation of B is set to be zero.

$\therefore$ $\frac{d[B]}{dt}=0$

For this reaction,

$A⟶_{R_{1}}^{k_{1}}B$

Rate of reaction for this reaction $(R_{1}) =$ $k_{1}[A]$

For this reaction,

$B⟶_{R_{2}}^{k_{2}}C$

Rate of reaction for this reaction $(R_{2}) =$ $k_{2}[B]$

Net rate of formation of B = $\frac{d[B]}{dt}$ $= R_{1} - R_{2}$

As $\frac{d[B]}{dt}=0$

$\therefore$ $R_{1} - R_{2} = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ $k_{1}[A]$ - $k_{2}[B]$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $[B]=\frac{k_{1}}{k_{2}}[A]$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot

text:
Which of the following compounds will show
the maximum 'enol' content?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Enol content is high when the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ group lies between two carbonyl groups, so that the enol is stabilised by conjugation and by an intramolecular hydrogen bond.

(A) Acetone has only one carbonyl group, so its enol content is negligible.

(B) The enol of acetylacetone, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})=\mathrm{CHCOCH}{}_{3}$, has its C=C conjugated with the second C=O and forms a six-membered intramolecular O–H···O=C hydrogen bond, so the enol form predominates (about 80%).

(C) and (D) In the ester and the amide, the lone pair of $-\mathrm{OC}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}$ or $-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$ is already delocalised into its own C=O (cross-conjugation), which makes that C=O a poorer partner for the enol's conjugation and hydrogen bond, so the enol content is much lower (ethyl acetoacetate about 8%, the amide less still).

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot

solution.body:
The substrate is 2-methyl-6-oxoheptanal, $\mathrm{OHC}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$. NaOH can form enolates at C-2 (next to CHO), at C-5 (the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ next to the ketone) and at C-7 (the ketone $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$).

The C-5 enolate attacking the CHO carbon (C-1) closes a five-membered ring (C-1 to C-5) onto the more electrophilic aldehyde carbonyl, so this intramolecular aldol is preferred. Attack by C-7 on CHO would form a seven-membered ring, and attack by the C-2 enolate on the ketone (options A and C) uses the weaker ketone electrophile.

The aldol product, 1-(2-hydroxy-3-methylcyclopentyl)ethan-1-one, dehydrates on heating to give the C=C between the acetyl-bearing carbon and the former CHO carbon, conjugated with the C=O.


[IMG]

The product is 1-(3-methylcyclopent-1-en-1-yl)ethan-1-one.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
If p is the momentum of the fastest electron
ejected from a metal surface after the irradiation
of light having wavelength $λ$, then for 1.5 p
momentum of the photoelectron, the
wavelength of the light should be:
(Assume kinetic energy of ejected
photoelectron to be very high in comparison
to work function)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From photoelectric effect,

E = $𝜙$ + KE

$\frac{hc}{λ}=𝜙+\frac{p^{2}}{2m}$ ................ (1)

Now when momentum = 1.5p then let wavelength = $λ_{1}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{hc}{λ_{1}}=𝜙+\frac{(1.5p)^{2}}{2m}$ ........... (2)

Given,

kinetic energy(KE) of ejected
photoelectron to be very high in comparison
to work function($𝜙$).

$\therefore$ We can neglect work function($𝜙$).

$\therefore$ Equation (1) and (2) becomes,

$\frac{hc}{λ}=\frac{p^{2}}{2m}$ ................ (1)

$\frac{hc}{λ_{1}}=\frac{(1.5p)^{2}}{2m}$ ........... (2)

Dividing (1) by (2) we get,

$\frac{λ_{1}}{λ}=\frac{p^{2}}{(1.5p)^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{λ_{1}}{λ}=\frac{4}{9}$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ_{1}=\frac{4}{9}λ$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot

text:
For the solution of the gases w, x, y and z in
water at 298K, the Henrys law constants $(K_{H})$
are 0.5, 2, 35 and 40 kbar, respectively. The
correct plot for the given data is :-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Henry's law expression,

$P_{$gas$} = K_{H}$ $\times$ $x_{$gas}

Here, $P_{$gas} = partial pressure of gas

$K_{H} =$ Henry’s law constant

$x_{$gas} = mole fraction of gas

$\because$ $x_{$gas$} = 1 - x_{H2}O$

$\therefore$ $P_{$gas$} = K_{H}$ $\times$ $(1 - x_{H2}O)$

$\Rightarrow$ $P_{$gas$} = K_{H} - K_{H}$ $\timesx_{H2}O$

By comparing this equation with y = mx + c,

$c = K_{H} =$ Intercept

$m = - K_{H} =$ slope

So in partial pressure vs mole fraction of water graph, which gas has more $K_{H}$  will have more intercept. Given $(K_{H})$
are 0.5, 2, 35 and 40 kbar for w, x, y, z respectively. So intercept of z should be the most and  should be the least.

As solpe is $= - K_{H}$, so slope shoul be negative for all the gases and w gas should have least negative slope and z should have highest negative slope.
